status: User accepted the 1 exact diagnostic sites on 2026-10-07. Focused qualification and its recorded limits are unchanged. Full RPM and native architecture qualification remain separate gates.
root_cause: GCC cannot connect the recognized array-segment builtin call with the producer’s integer-constant input contract, so it treats the ignored matcher return as a potentially uninitialized output.
source_review: ArrayNewSegment emits Word32Constant(segment_imm.index) as its first builtin argument. IsArrayNewSegment recognizes that exact builtin after unwrapping optional type and nonthrowing-operation annotations.
MatchIntegralWord32Constant initializes its output for a Word32 constant; StringNewWtf8ArrayImpl consumes that initialized output.
ValidateDataSegment rejects indexes outside num_declared_data_segments. The decoder caps this count at 100000, so every valid index fits the tagged small-integer range.

Release/debug normally and under Valgrind.
coverage.compiler: Both modes reproduce index_val; no additional diagnostics.
coverage.memory: Both qualified runs have zero errors and all allocations freed.
coverage.actual_wasm: Real array.new_data plus string.new_wtf8_array modules, with baseline compiler disabled, validate eight distinct segments: empty, ASCII, NUL, two/four-byte UTF-8, lone surrogate, mixed string and malformed encoding. Check complete/subrange decoding, empty ranges, reversed/out-of-range indexes and invalid segment compile rejection.

Actual Wasm tests exercise eight segment indexes; larger validated indexes are covered by the native producer/matcher control and decoder bounds review.
